analysis:
All three changed files are CI workflows, and the diffs touch no provider runtime, WebSocket, attestation or encryption code. No runtime threat ID (A-001..A-020, TB-002..TB-014, T-0xx) is affected. T-041 and the prefix-cache paths are untouched.

Changes examined:
1. provider-plan.yml: lane table edits only. The Cluster GPU shards and the build jobs now always ask the route for a lane, with sizes. The request is `test-cluster-gpu-{shard}`, and the GPU shards are no longer pinned to Blacksmith. Contents permissions remain read-only and the route job has `permissions: {}`. The lane sizes are an availability and cost question, not a security one. In particular, shard 2 previously needed more memory than any signed size and now asks for 4x24, so it may fail. Those shards are non-blocking.
2. provider-release-cache.yml and provider-tests.yml: a new first step, 'Choose this job's Actions cache', sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off in GITHUB_ENV when a Darkbloom runner (runner name `darkbloom-*`) has no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. Every actions/cache restore and save step in provider-tests.yml is gated on that variable. The gating matches the stated intent: it keeps a Darkbloom sandbox from reaching GitHub's own Actions cache. The variable is only ever set to 'off', and runner-controlled values are only echoed. I found no injection. The RUNNER_NAME check relies on the runner's own naming, which is expected. In provider-release-cache.yml the new step is added, but the file's cache steps live in the composite action, which is not supplied. Whether that action honours CI_ACTIONS_CACHE is unverified.
3. provider-tests.yml 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git': new pre-checkout validation rejects a .git that is a symlink or not a directory, holds any symlink, holds a non-sample hook (case-insensitive path match), or whose config files set core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeIf. It then runs the fsck check. This is purely additive hardening over the base, which only ran fsck. It is a denylist, so it does not cover other config keys that execute commands or can be abused (core.sshCommand, filter.*.clean/smudge/process, core.pager, credential.helper, diff.external, gpg.program). The comment 'runs nothing' therefore overclaims. This is a residual risk from pre-existing Actions cache poisoning, not a regression.

Open integration questions: how Darkbloom cache scoping and isolation between PR and master is enforced (plane side, unsupplied), and whether composite actions and other workflows apply the same CI_ACTIONS_CACHE gating. No security regression is identified in the supplied evidence.
